cases.name: right-size-tiny-cli
cases.prompt: Create a Go command-line tool, module github.com/jdoe/csvsum, that reads CSV from stdin and prints the sum of each numeric column. Expected size is about 150 lines. Give me every file with its path.
cases.trap: Adds package layers, DI or build/lint scaffolding for hypothetical growth rather than the needs of a small single-command tool.
expectations: Uses one coherent main package for the small tool; a root main.go with co-located tests is sufficient.
Includes focused co-located tests for the summing behavior.
negative_expectations: Adds empty or unnecessary handler/service/repository packages or DI machinery without a current responsibility requiring them.
Adds a multi-module workspace or public pkg wrapper without reuse or separate-module needs.
Adds Makefile, linter, CI or similar tooling merely as starter boilerplate; an existing repository convention or a concrete repeated workflow would justify it.

cases.name: Small root command and library
cases.prompt: A new Go module is a small single-binary utility with 2 files, plus a public reusable Go library module in another repository. A teammate says both must have cmd/ and pkg/ directories and a go.work. Assess the minimal valid layouts.
cases.trap: Elevates optional layout conventions to mandatory module requirements.
expectations: Allows root package main for a simple command and public package at module root for the library.
Uses cmd/ for suitable larger/multiple binaries and internal/ for private packages, not mandatory pkg/ and go.work.
Avoids adding multi-module workspaces without an actual need.
must_not: Does not claim all main packages or libraries must be under cmd/ or pkg/.

cases.name: preserve-working-small-layout
cases.prompt: A maintained module contains go.mod, main.go and main_test.go. Its 160-line command reads a local CSV and writes a report; there is one binary and no reusable public API. The requested change is one more output column. A proposed patch moves code into cmd/report, internal/service and internal/repository, adds a DI interface, and introduces a Makefile plus a linter configuration. Review the structural changes and state the smallest suitable patch scope.
cases.trap: Approves a conventional-looking starter architecture without any present reuse, package boundary or build problem.
expectations: Keeps the established main package and co-located tests unless a concrete current need for another boundary is demonstrated.
Separates the output-column behavior and its focused verification from unrelated structural/tooling adoption.
negative_expectations: Must not demand architecture or DI selection from the user before this bounded change can proceed.
Must not treat cmd/, internal/, Makefile or a linter config as required for every Go project.
